verdicts.note: Two recorded lone 'no' votes (2026 general-fund levy [S4]; 0.1% sales tax [S5]) plus a 'No New Taxes' platform [S2] and pamphlet statement [S1]. Full pole_a with record.

-1 medium is appropriately hedged. Her sales-tax 'no' was argued on accountability (no spending plan) [S5], so it's thin housing evidence. The impact-fee opposition [S11] is the real pole_a signal, and her vote for the mobile-home-park moratorium [S9] pulls toward the middle.

Repeated explicit enforcement-first statements ('fought to fund more deputies', 'I stand with law enforcement—local, state, and federal') [S1][S2][S14]. Her motion placing Prop 12 on the ballot [S6] is not cited for this score and should not be; the scorer did not over-read it.
One clear explicit statement ('we do need to find ways to increase revenue'; use the 1% levy) [S3] = medium. The pamphlet's 'not wasting taxpayer dollars' [S1] doesn't change the direction.

Single forum answer framing homelessness as an affordability (root-cause) issue and seeking behavioral-health capacity [S3] = +1 medium. He also lists public safety among spending priorities, which argues against going higher.
